```python
script_content = '''import json
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from openpyxl import load_workbook
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH

# ── Step 1: Read Excel ──
EXCEL_PATH = "/workspace/testbed/data/order_summary.xlsx"
wb = load_workbook(EXCEL_PATH)
ws = wb.active

rows = []
headers = None
for i, row in enumerate(ws.iter_rows(values_only=True)):
    if i == 0:
        headers = [str(c) if c is not None else f"col_{j}" for j, c in enumerate(row)]
    else:
        rows.append(dict(zip(headers, row)))

print(f"Loaded {len(rows)} orders with columns: {headers}")

# ── Step 2: Compute statistics ──
total_orders = len(rows)

# Amounts
amounts = []
for r in rows:
    try:
        amounts.append(float(r.get("Total Paid", 0)))
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        pass

total_revenue = round(sum(amounts), 2)
avg_order = round(total_revenue / len(amounts), 2) if amounts else 0
max_order = round(max(amounts), 2) if amounts else 0
min_order = round(min(amounts), 2) if amounts else 0
sorted_a = sorted(amounts)
median_order = round(sorted_a[len(sorted_a) // 2], 2) if sorted_a else 0

# Status breakdown
status_counts = Counter(str(r.get("Status", "Unknown")) for r in rows)

# Customer breakdown
customer_counts = Counter(str(r.get("Customer", "Unknown")) for r in rows)
customer_revenue = defaultdict(float)
for r in rows:
    try:
        customer_revenue[str(r.get("Customer", "Unknown"))] += float(r.get("Total Paid", 0))
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        pass

# Item popularity (split comma-separated items)
item_counts = Counter()
for r in rows:
    items_str = str(r.get("Items", ""))
    for item in items_str.split(", "):
        item = item.strip()
        if item:
            item_counts[item] += 1

# Date breakdown
date_counts = Counter(str(r.get("Date", "Unknown")) for r in rows)

print(f"\\nTotal orders: {total_orders}")
print(f"Total revenue: ${total_revenue:,.2f}")
print(f"Avg order value: ${avg_order:,.2f}")
print(f"Max order: ${max_order:,.2f}, Min order: ${min_order:,.2f}, Median: ${median_order:,.2f}")
print(f"Status breakdown: {dict(status_counts.most_common())}")
print(f"Unique customers: {len(customer_counts)}")
print(f"Top 5 customers by orders: {dict(customer_counts.most_common(5))}")
print(f"Top 5 customers by revenue: {dict(sorted(customer_revenue.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])[:5])}")
print(f"Top 10 items: {dict(item_counts.most_common(10))}")
print(f"Orders by date: {dict(date_counts.most_common())}")

# ── Step 3: Build Word Document ──
WORD_PATH = "/workspace/testbed/docs/order_analysis.docx"
doc = Document()

# Title
title_para = doc.add_heading("Order Summary Analysis Report", level=0)
title_para.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER

doc.add_paragraph("")

# Section 1: Overview
doc.add_heading("1. Overview", level=1)
doc.add_paragraph(
    f"This report presents an analysis of {total_orders} orders from the order_summary.xlsx dataset. "
    f"The orders span {len(date_counts)} date(s) and involve {len(customer_counts)} unique customers. "
    f"The total revenue across all orders is ${total_revenue:,.2f}."
)

# Section 2: Key Metrics
doc.add_heading("2. Key Metrics", level=1)
table = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=2)
table.style = "Light Shading Accent 1"
hdr = table.rows[0].cells
hdr[0].text = "Metric"
hdr[1].text = "Value"

metrics = [
    ("Total Orders", str(total_orders)),
    ("Total Revenue", f"${total_revenue:,.2f}"),
    ("Average Order Value", f"${avg_order:,.2f}"),
    ("Highest Order", f"${max_order:,.2f}"),
    ("Lowest Order", f"${min_order:,.2f}"),
    ("Median Order Value", f"${median_order:,.2f}"),
    ("Unique Customers", str(len(customer_counts))),
    ("Unique Products", str(len(item_counts))),
]
for m, v in metrics:
    rc = table.add_row().cells
    rc[0].text = m
    rc[1].text = v

# Section 3: Order Status Breakdown
doc.add_heading("3. Order Status Breakdown", level=1)
t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=2)
t.style = "Light Shading Accent 1"
t.rows[0].cells[0].text = "Status"
t.rows[0].cells[1].text = "Count"
for s, c in status_counts.most_common():
    rc = t.add_row().cells
    rc[0].text = str(s).capitalize()
    rc[1].text = str(c)

# Section 4: Top Customers by Revenue
doc.add_heading("4. Top Customers by Revenue", level=1)
t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=3)
t.style = "Light Shading Accent 1"
t.rows[0].cells[0].text = "Customer"
t.rows[0].cells[1].text = "Orders"
t.rows[0].cells[2].text = "Total Spent"
for cust, rev in sorted(customer_revenue.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])[:10]:
    rc = t.add_row().cells
    rc[0].text = str(cust)
    rc[1].text = str(customer_counts[cust])
    rc[2].text = f"${rev:,.2f}"

# Section 5: Most Popular Products
doc.add_heading("5. Most Popular Products", level=1)
t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=2)
t.style = "Light Shading Accent 1"
t.rows[0].cells[0].text = "Product"
t.rows[0].cells[1].text = "Appearances"
for item, cnt in item_counts.most_common(10):
    rc = t.add_row().cells
    rc[0].text = str(item)
    rc[1].text = str(cnt)

# Section 6: Orders by Date
doc.add_heading("6. Orders by Date", level=1)
t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=2)
t.style = "Light Shading Accent 1"
t.rows[0].cells[0].text = "Date"
t.rows[0].cells[1].text = "Order Count"
for d, cnt in sorted(date_counts.items()):
    rc = t.add_row().cells
    rc[0].text = str(d)
    rc[1].text = str(cnt)

# Section 7: Summary
doc.add_heading("7. Summary", level=1)
top_product = item_counts.most_common(1)[0] if item_counts else ("N/A", 0)
top_customer = sorted(customer_revenue.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])[0] if customer_revenue else ("N/A", 0)
confirmed = status_counts.get("confirmed", 0)
cancelled = status_counts.get("cancelled", 0)

doc.add_paragraph(
    f"Of the {total_orders} orders analyzed, {confirmed} were confirmed and {cancelled} were cancelled, "
    f"yielding a confirmation rate of {confirmed/total_orders*100:.1f}%. "
    f"The most popular product was \\"{top_product[0]}\\" appearing in {top_product[1]} orders. "
    f"The top customer by revenue was \\"{top_customer[0]}\\" with ${top_customer[1]:,.2f} in total spending. "
    f"The average order value was ${avg_order:,.2f}, with orders ranging from ${min_order:,.2f} to ${max_order:,.2f}."
)

doc.save(WORD_PATH)
print(f"\\nWord document saved to {WORD_PATH}")
print("DONE")
'''
write_result = await write_file("./build_report.py", script_content)
print(write_result)

run_result = await run_command("python ./build_report.py")
print(run_result)

verify_doc = await run_command("python3 skills/OfficeBench/tools/word/read_file.py --file_path /workspace/testbed/docs/order_analysis.docx")
print(verify_doc)
```
